quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and cars already in the roundabout.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you must always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Obey all traffic signals.
Watch for pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars, motorcycles, and bicyclists.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. You may complete your turn once the intersection is clear and the signal allows it.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: One lane ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, such as school buses and hazardous material trucks.
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space when following a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle stops suddenly or the rider falls. Motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: If a vehicle skids on water, the driver should quickly apply the brakes.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids while hydroplaning, try to regain control. If you cannot, release the accelerator and ride out the skid. Do not apply the brakes suddenly.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or when they do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes distorted.
You are less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your ability to handle headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly to give approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know you are coming.
Must stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians crossing. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. Not stopping is against the law.

questions.question: When in a travel lane on the roadway:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may turn around or back up if you take the wrong freeway entrance.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely leave the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Drive to the next turn or exit instead.

questions.question: It is more dangerous to drive at night than during the day because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always slippier at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, poor visibility and glare from oncoming headlights make it hard to see ahead. Always use your headlights and be extra careful when driving in the dark.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
How fast you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. It may frustrate drivers behind you, causing them to make risky passes. It is safest to drive with the flow of traffic and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction due to water on the road, you should:

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to get better traction.
Apply the brakes hard to stop your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: In heavy rain, your tires can lose contact with the road and ride on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.

questions.question: If you are driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind resistance on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means vehicles in both directions can pass. You may only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves to the right and then to the left.
The road ahead curves to the left and then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves to the right and then to the left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign is used with a traffic signal. It tells drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way and must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the hardest driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Using snow tires is the best option for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or similar bad conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season and requires extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve your vehicle's grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: Sudden wind gusts on highways can affect:

options.text: Only large vehicles.
Only visibility.
All vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can affect all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust and dirt on the road. It can also physically move a vehicle.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep the same speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the same speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not speed up or brake. Keep your speed steady so the other vehicle can safely pass and merge back into your lane.

questions.question: A red curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
Pickup or drop-off area for passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Keep your tires properly inflated.
Slow down when driving in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tire tread in good condition and inflate your tires correctly. Slow down when it rains. Hydroplaning happens more often at high speeds.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and be careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of a hazard. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: "No zones" around trucks are areas where cars:

options.text: Cannot be seen by the truck driver or are too close for the truck to stop and turn safely.
Have enough space to drive behind the truck.
Are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be seen by the truck driver or are too close for the truck to stop and turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks where cars disappear from view. They are also areas where a car is so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "no zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Cars have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Yield means stop if you cannot safely merge into traffic.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When you must yield the right-of-way, you must also stop if you cannot safely merge into traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Go through carefully without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop where you can see oncoming traffic. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: At night, when an oncoming vehicle approaches, your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off, with only parking lights on.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another vehicle is approaching or when you are following a vehicle. Use low beams to keep everyone safe.
